item.title: Cognition
item.description:
Machine?

If you came to the realization that everything you ever did was simply mechanical, would you accept that you lived a true life of a machine?

AI is Coming

Some frightening things are happening with AI. And perhaps we should be frightened.

Not because these machines are conscious, or because I believe that, as they become more sophisticated, they will somehow awaken into consciousness. I don’t. What I do not doubt is that they will become more and more intelligent—perhaps unimaginably so.

item.title: Customs
item.description:
rAvaNa dies again

Ravana Dies Again

I remember asking my father after watching Ramlila twice: but they already killed Ravana last year and why did they kill him again? And my father said: you, son, have to kill Ravana again and again till the end of time. I simply failed to comprehend his statement and even forgot about this conversation. After five decades, I came to realize its depth and fathom meaning of repeated death of Ravana.

item.title: Gods
item.description:
All-knowing

Today I am having compassion for the being that is said to be all-knowing. and this compassion extends also to my philosopher colleagues who have extensively worked on omniscience. For every fact, there are millions of fabrications. One cannot actually know what love is like without experiencing it first hand. But what about hate? But I am more worried about knowing things like infinity. I do not think that all-knowing entity has not fathomed it, but then that would be finite. i am perfectly fine to remain ignorant than to know the hair count in every single rat ball, past and future.

item.title: Life
item.description:
The Order

I remember not being able to articulate the ṛ phoneme, and so when the old man said, “ṛtaṃ ca satyaṃ ca,” I said, ’litam ca satyaṃ ca."+++(4)+++ I must have been four or five. I never thought of what they meant. I was supposed to sing these old songs so many times that every cell in my body was supposed to savor the memory. It was not reciting the mantras but reliving the recollections of hundreds of generations.

item.title: Money
item.description:
I have observed that even after joining the billionaire’s club, a pauper still remains a pauper.

The discovery of God

When the aliens encountered a lost civilization on the blue planet, they discovered a giant monolith with the writings “In God We Trust.” They were able to relate to most of the human concepts but the term God did not resemble any of their concepts. All their historians, anthropologists, archaeologists, philosophers and sociologists vested their energy to comprehend the signature concept that they found alien.

item.title: Other people
item.description:
How to make friends on Facebook:

  1. Immediately unfriend those who tag you by clicking on ‘Followers.’
  2. Wish your friends a happy birthday. If you feel awkward because you never interacted with them, unfriend them.
  3. Immediately unfriend those who share politically motivated, biased opinions.
  4. Unfriend those who are not active on Facebook. There are other ways to maintain friendship with them.
  5. Unfriend those who do not reply to your messages.
  6. Now you’ve got the point. Find ten additional reasons, and you will find your friends.

Trust

To trust is to make yourself vulnerable.
And nobody likes that.
But all our social transactions are based on trust,
and so we seek that people trust us.
To trust is therefore to live in a perpetual dilemma of being shattered.

item.title: paNDits
item.description:
Arvind Sharma

I am very sorry to share with you that Professor Arvind Sharma has departed from this world. He has been the greatest source of inspiration for many among us, including myself. May his wisdom continue to inspire us all, and may all of us make his memory a celebration of Mother Sarasvati.

And the Books Were Released

Everyone felt the pressure. The editors, the friends writing introductions, the cover designers—no one had a moment to breathe. I had made up my mind: I would publish all eight of my Sanskrit works, no matter how incomplete they might seem. I was no longer willing to wait.

item.title: Places
item.description:
The Magic Trail

It has been a while I have been reminiscing some of the trails that I traversed when I was young. They say we leave our footprints behind. I do not believe that. What I believe is the trails leave their imprints on our mind and the I that I experience as myself becomes integral to the trails that I took in different modes of time. The trails do not care for our footprints. They become alive in our memory though.

item.title: Politics
item.description:
Shorts

Long ago in Nepal, people elected their leader by a marathon. Inspired by this, I believe we can have a similar system. Rather than a race, we should let the best comedian win.

In Defense of Her Majesty

It is ridiculous for me to reconsider monarchy after four decades, as the first time I marched in the streets of Kathmandu against monarchy, I was just a teenager. But then, I had not watched The Truman Show; it was not even made. Hollywood did exist, but I had not read Baudrillard. I did attend some carnivals but nobody even mentioned Bakhtin. My support is not for power but for grandiose, for extravagance and for the simulacra. With the royals around, we all can appreciate the Lorde within each of us.

item.title: Shorts
item.description:
Masks

There are moments when the mask fails to hide the face behind.

Books

Books, I think, are like fruit trees. As long as you take care of them, they keep giving new fruits every new season.

right and left

there was this guy named empire with massive manhood. he named his two balls right and left.

item.title: Teachers
item.description:
Awakening

I have met a few awakened people in my life. Some were rather vocal about their awakening. A few years later, I found some of them in rehab. Others believed sincerely in enlightenment as a project, something to be pursued with discipline and determination. They savored every act of virtue as another step toward the ultimate destination. Enlightenment had become a horizon against which they measured their lives.

I was among those who never took up enlightenment as a project. I had no systematic pursuit, no carefully laid path toward awakening. And yet, there were moments.

item.title: Tech
item.description:
Are you human?

Every time I log onto something, I am asked serious questions, like right now, I am reviewing a paper for a journal and the system asks me to click, “I am a human.” Often times, I have been asked to confirm, I am not a robot. Is there any room left for the skeptics like myself in this world?

Liking

Facebook is making our concept of liking very shallow. When I clicked like for one page it said I already liked it. There is no room for me to like the same thing again and again. Well this says all about the Facebook likes.

item.title: Transcendence
item.description:
Shorts

Every society or civilization is founded on myth. It is not the power of truth but of myth that keeps the culture alive. The first liberation is to free oneself from these constructions.

Freedom

It is the inner drive, a surge of being that overpowers the conditions of us being in whichever states. This is not a judgment upon something, this is not a philosophy or politics. We do not explore freedom, it is the other way around. It is the freedom that has found us and freedom will keep finding all the new forms.

item.title: Word
item.description:
Poetic vision

We are woven twice, in two different layers of our being. The first is when the being or sat expressed itself, it being manifest as mantras. We then were the songs articulated by the first poet, Brahmā. But his poetry lacked shades and needed more colors to be infused. His grandson Shukra made it possible, weaving the threads, the chandas, once again. His love for Divyā, a demon princess with a divine name, explains the paradox behind this poetic vision. Sapped with his vigor and lust, poetry came to life, with the lineage of both gods and demons. We can still distill the mantras of the grandfather in the songs of Shukra.
